license_required.quote: A person who, not being licensed, advertises or holds himself or herself out to the public as described in section 1311 of this title, or who, not being licensed, practices medicine as defined in section 1311 of this title, or who practices medicine under a fictitious or assumed name, or who impersonates another practitioner or who is not a licensed health care professional as defined in 18 V.S.A. § 5202 and signs a certificate of death for the purpose of burial or removal, shall be imprisoned not more than two years or fined not more than $10,000.00, or both.

issuing_authority.quote: The Board of Medical Practice is created.

name.quote: The Board of Medical Practice is created.

type.quote: The Board shall be composed of 17 members, nine of whom shall be licensed physicians, one of whom shall be a physician assistant licensed pursuant to chapter 31 of this title, one of whom shall be a podiatrist licensed pursuant to chapter 7 of this title, and six of whom shall be persons not associated with the medical field.

umbrella_agency.quote: The Board of Medical Practice is established as an office within the Department of Health.

moral_character_required.quote: is of sound moral character and professional competence as evidenced by

accrediting_body.quote: a medical school accredited by an organization that is acceptable to the Board, or from a medical school that has been approved by the Board by rule

degree_level.quote: with a degree of doctor of medicine or an equivalent as may be determined by the Board

exams.name: Medical licensing examination (as established by Board rule)
exams.notes: The Board may identify which examinations are accepted, set passing standards, and set limits on time and numbers of attempts. The USMLE and COMLEX-USA are referenced in the Interstate Medical Licensure Compact provisions.
exams.jurisdiction: as established by the Board by rule
exams.quote: An applicant shall satisfy the Board's requirements for medical licensing examination as established by the Board by rule. The Board may identify which examinations are accepted, set passing standards, and set limits on time and numbers of attempts for exams.

exams.name: United States Medical Licensing Examination (USMLE)
exams.notes: Referenced as a qualifying exam for Interstate Medical Licensure Compact eligibility; must be passed within three attempts.

exams.notes: Referenced as an alternative qualifying exam for Interstate Medical Licensure Compact eligibility; must be passed within three attempts.
exams.quote: passed each component of the United States Medical Licensing Examination (USMLE) or the Comprehensive Osteopathic Medical Licensing Examination (COMLEX-USA) within three attempts

interval_years.citation: § 1400. Renewal of license; continuing medical education

required.quote: A licensee for renewal of an active license to practice medicine shall have completed continuing medical education that shall meet minimum criteria as established by rule, by the Board
required.citation: § 1400. Renewal of license; continuing medical education

hours_per_period.quote: The Board shall require a minimum of 10 hours of continuing medical education by rule.
hours_per_period.citation: § 1400. Renewal of license; continuing medical education

period_years.quote: Every person licensed to practice medicine by the Board shall apply biennially for the renewal of his or her license.

advances in other fields for which patient referrals may be appropriate
current professional competence in recognizing the need for timely appropriate consultations and referrals

topical_requirements.quote: The training provided by the continuing medical education shall be designed to assure that the licensee has updated his or her knowledge and skills in his or her own specialties and also has kept abreast of advances in other fields for which patient referrals may be appropriate. The Board shall require evidence of current professional competence in recognizing the need for timely appropriate consultations and referrals to assure fully informed patient choice of treatment options, including treatments such as those offered by hospice, palliative care, and pain management services.
topical_requirements.citation: § 1400. Renewal of license; continuing medical education

available.quote: The Board shall have an endorsement process for physician licensure that requires not more than three years of practice in good standing in another jurisdiction within the United States, regardless of whether that jurisdiction has licensing requirements substantially equal to those of this State

requirements.value: Applicant must have practiced in good standing in another U.S. jurisdiction for not more than three years, and must meet postgraduate training requirements (2 years for U.S./Canadian graduates, 3 years for foreign graduates). The Board may waive the practice requirement if consistent with State policy and public protection.
requirements.quote: The Board shall have an endorsement process for physician licensure that requires not more than three years of practice in good standing in another jurisdiction within the United States, regardless of whether that jurisdiction has licensing requirements substantially equal to those of this State, provided the applicant meets one of the following postgraduate training requirements

national_certification.quote: A graduate of a medical school outside the United States or Canada shall also submit evidence of certification by the Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates

national_association.quote: a physician who is Board-certified or Board-eligible in his or her field of specialty, as determined by the American Board of Medical Specialties (ABMS)

regulatory_model.quote: A person who, not being licensed, advertises or holds himself or herself out to the public as described in section 1311 of this title, or who, not being licensed, practices medicine as defined in section 1311 of this title, or who practices medicine under a fictitious or assumed name, or who impersonates another practitioner or who is not a licensed health care professional as defined in 18 V.S.A. § 5202 and signs a certificate of death for the purpose of burial or removal, shall be imprisoned not more than two years or fined not more than $10,000.00, or both.

credential_type.quote: License and certify health professionals pursuant to this title.
credential_type.citation: § 1353. Powers and duties of the Board

is_mandatory.quote: A person who, not being licensed, advertises or holds himself or herself out to the public as described in section 1311 of this title, or who, not being licensed, practices medicine as defined in section 1311 of this title, or who practices medicine under a fictitious or assumed name, or who impersonates another practitioner or who is not a licensed health care professional as defined in 18 V.S.A. § 5202 and signs a certificate of death for the purpose of burial or removal, shall be imprisoned not more than two years or fined not more than $10,000.00, or both.

title_protection.quote: using the designation "Doctor," "Doctor of Medicine," "Physician," "Dr.," "M.D.," or any combination thereof in the conduct of any occupation or profession pertaining to the prevention, diagnosis, or treatment of human disease or condition unless the designation additionally contains the description of another branch of the healing arts for which one holds a valid license in Vermont

scope_protection.quote: A person who, not being licensed, advertises or holds himself or herself out to the public as described in section 1311 of this title, or who, not being licensed, practices medicine as defined in section 1311 of this title, or who practices medicine under a fictitious or assumed name, or who impersonates another practitioner or who is not a licensed health care professional as defined in 18 V.S.A. § 5202 and signs a certificate of death for the purpose of burial or removal, shall be imprisoned not more than two years or fined not more than $10,000.00, or both.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Fraud or misrepresentation in applying for or procuring a medical license or its renewal.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: fraud or misrepresentation in applying for or procuring a medical license or in connection with applying for or procuring periodic renewal of a medical license

disciplinary_grounds.description: Advertising about health care services intended or tending to mislead or deceive the public.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: all advertising about health care services or a medical business that is intended or has a tendency to mislead or deceive the public or impose upon credulous or ignorant persons and so be harmful or injurious to public morals or safety

disciplinary_grounds.description: Abandonment of a patient.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: abandonment of a patient

disciplinary_grounds.description: Habitual or excessive use or abuse of drugs, alcohol, or other substances that impair the licensee's ability to practice medicine.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: habitual or excessive use or abuse of drugs, alcohol, or other substances that impair the licensee's ability to practice medicine

disciplinary_grounds.description: Promotion of sale of drugs or devices in a manner that exploits the patient for financial gain, or prescribing drugs for non-therapeutic purposes.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: promotion by a physician of the sale of drugs, devices, appliances, or goods provided for a patient in such a manner as to exploit the patient for financial gain of the physician or selling, prescribing, giving away, or administering drugs for other than legal and legitimate therapeutic purposes

disciplinary_grounds.description: Conduct that evidences unfitness to practice medicine.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: conduct that evidences unfitness to practice medicine

disciplinary_grounds.description: Willfully making and filing false reports or records in practice as a physician.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: willfully making and filing false reports or records in his or her practice as a physician

disciplinary_grounds.description: Willful omission to file or record, or impeding the filing of, medical reports required by law.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: willful omission to file or record, or willfully impeding or obstructing a filing or recording, or inducing another person to omit to file or record medical reports required by law

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to make patient records promptly available upon proper written request.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: failure to make available promptly to a person using professional health care services, that person's representative, succeeding health care professionals, or institutions, when given proper written request and direction of the person using professional health care services, copies of that person's records in the possession or under the control of the licensed practitioner

disciplinary_grounds.description: Solicitation of professional patronage by agents or profiting from acts of those representing themselves as agents.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: solicitation of professional patronage by agents or persons or profiting from the acts of those representing themselves to be agents of the licensed physician

disciplinary_grounds.description: Division of fees or agreeing to split fees for referrals.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: division of fees or agreeing to split or divide the fees received for professional services for any person for bringing to or referring a patient

disciplinary_grounds.description: Agreeing with laboratories to make payments for tests without disclosing the arrangement to patients or payors.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: agreeing with clinical or bio-analytical laboratories to make payments to such laboratories for individual tests or test series for patients, unless the physician discloses on the bills to patients or third party payors the name of such laboratory, the amount or amounts to such laboratory for individual tests or test series, and the amount of his or her processing charge or procurement, if any, for each specimen taken

disciplinary_grounds.description: Willful misrepresentation in treatments.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: willful misrepresentation in treatments

disciplinary_grounds.description: Practicing medicine with a physician who is not legally practicing within the State, or aiding such physician.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: practicing medicine with a physician who is not legally practicing within the State, or aiding or abetting such physician in the practice of medicine

disciplinary_grounds.description: Gross overcharging for professional services on repeated occasions, including filing false statements for collection of fees for services not rendered.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: gross overcharging for professional services on repeated occasions, including filing of false statements for collection of fees for which services are not rendered

disciplinary_grounds.description: Offering, undertaking, or agreeing to cure or treat disease by a secret method, procedure, treatment, or medicine.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: offering, undertaking, or agreeing to cure or treat disease by a secret method, procedure, treatment, or medicine

disciplinary_grounds.description: Consistent improper utilization of services.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: consistent improper utilization of services

disciplinary_grounds.description: Consistent use of nonaccepted procedures that have a consistent detrimental effect upon patients.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: consistent use of nonaccepted procedures that have a consistent detrimental effect upon patients

disciplinary_grounds.description: Professional incompetency resulting from physical or mental impairment.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: professional incompetency resulting from physical or mental impairment

disciplinary_grounds.description: Permitting one's name or license to be used by a person, group, or corporation when not actually in charge of or overseeing the health care services provided.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: permitting one's name or license to be used by a person, group, or corporation when not actually in charge of, responsible for, or actively overseeing the treatment or other health care services provided

disciplinary_grounds.description: Gross failure or repeated failure to use the degree of care, skill, and proficiency commonly exercised by the ordinary skillful, careful, and prudent physician.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: in the course of practice, gross failure to use and exercise on a particular occasion or the failure to use and exercise on repeated occasions, that degree of care, skill, and proficiency that is commonly exercised by the ordinary skillful, careful, and prudent physician engaged in similar practice under the same or similar conditions, whether or not actual injury to a patient has occurred

disciplinary_grounds.description: Revocation of a license or other disciplinary sanction by another jurisdiction on grounds specified in this section.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: revocation of a license to practice medicine or surgery, or other disciplinary sanction, by another jurisdiction on one or more of the grounds specified in this section

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to comply with an order of the Board or violation of any term or condition of a restricted or conditioned license.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: failure to comply with an order of the Board or violation of any term or condition of a license that is restricted or conditioned by the Board

disciplinary_grounds.description: Allowing a nurse practitioner to perform a medical act outside the usual scope of the physician's own practice or for which the nurse practitioner is not qualified.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: any physician who, in the course of a collaborative agreement with a nurse practitioner allows the nurse practitioner to perform a medical act that is outside the usual scope of the physician's own practice or that the nurse practitioner is not qualified to perform by training or experience

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to comply with federal or state statutes or rules governing the practice of medicine or surgery.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: failure to comply with provisions of federal statutes or regulations, or the statutes or rules of this or any other state, governing the practice of medicine or surgery

disciplinary_grounds.description: Practice of profession when medically or psychologically unfit to do so.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: practice of profession when medically or psychologically unfit to do so

disciplinary_grounds.description: Delegation of professional responsibilities to a person not qualified by training, experience, education, or licensing credentials.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: delegation of professional responsibilities, including delivery of any health care services, to a person whom the licensed professional knows, or has reason to know, is not qualified by training, experience, education, or licensing credentials to perform them

disciplinary_grounds.description: Conviction of a crime related to the practice of the profession or conviction of a felony, or failure to report such conviction to the Board within 30 days.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: conviction of a crime related to the practice of the profession or conviction of a felony, whether or not related to the practice of the profession, or failure to report to the Board a conviction of any crime related to the practice of the profession or any felony in any court within 30 days of the conviction

disciplinary_grounds.description: Use of the services of an anesthesiologist assistant in a manner inconsistent with chapter 29 of this title.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: use of the services of an anesthesiologist assistant by an anesthesiologist in a manner that is inconsistent with the provisions of chapter 29 of this title

disciplinary_grounds.description: Use of the services of a radiologist assistant in a manner inconsistent with chapter 52 of this title.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: use of the services of a radiologist assistant by a radiologist in a manner that is inconsistent with the provisions of chapter 52 of this title

disciplinary_grounds.description: Providing medical services or prescription medication via electronic means without establishing a proper physician-patient relationship.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: providing, prescribing, dispensing, or furnishing medical services or prescription medication or prescription-only devices to a person in response to any communication transmitted or received by computer or other electronic means, when the licensee fails to take the following actions to establish and maintain a proper physician-patient relationship

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to provide to the Board information it may reasonably request in furtherance of its statutory duties.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: failure to provide to the Board such information it may reasonably request in furtherance of its statutory duties

disciplinary_grounds.description: Disruptive behavior involving interaction with physicians, hospital personnel, office staff, patients, or others that interferes with patient care.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: disruptive behavior that involves interaction with physicians, hospital personnel, office staff, patients, or support persons of the patient or others that interferes with patient care or could reasonably be expected to adversely affect the quality of care rendered to a patient

disciplinary_grounds.description: Commission of any sexual misconduct that exploits the physician-patient relationship, including sexual contact with a patient.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: commission of any sexual misconduct that exploits the physician-patient relationship, including sexual contact with a patient, surrogates, or key third parties

disciplinary_grounds.description: Prescribing, selling, administering, distributing, ordering, or dispensing any controlled substance for the licensee's own use or to an immediate family member.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: prescribing, selling, administering, distributing, ordering, or dispensing any drug legally classified as a controlled substance for the licensee's own use or to an immediate family member as defined by rule

disciplinary_grounds.description: Signing a blank or undated prescription form.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: signing a blank or undated prescription form

disciplinary_grounds.description: Use of conversion therapy on a client younger than 18 years of age.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: use of conversion therapy as defined in 18 V.S.A. § 8351 on a client younger than 18 years of age

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to comply with notice, disclosure, or advertising requirements for administering unapproved stem cell products.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: failure to comply with one or more of the notice, disclosure, or advertising requirements in 18 V.S.A. § 4502 for administering stem cell or stem cell-related products not approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to practice competently, including performance of unsafe or unacceptable patient care or failure to conform to essential standards of acceptable and prevailing practice.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: failure to practice competently by reason of any cause on a single occasion or on multiple occasions constitutes unprofessional conduct. Failure to practice competently includes, as determined by the Board: (1) performance of unsafe or unacceptable patient care; or (2) failure to conform to the essential standards of acceptable and prevailing practice.

foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.value: A graduate of a medical school outside the United States or Canada must complete at least three years of postgraduate training in a U.S. or Canadian accredited program (vs. two years for U.S./Canadian graduates) and must submit evidence of certification by the Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates (ECFMG), unless qualifying as a Fifth Pathway applicant.
foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.quote: A graduate of a Board-approved medical school outside the United States or Canada shall submit evidence of success of completing at least three years of postgraduate training in a U.S. or Canadian program accredited by an organization that is acceptable to the Board

postgraduate_training_years_required.quote: A graduate of a U.S. or Canadian medical school accredited by a body that is acceptable to the Board shall submit evidence of the successful completion of at least two years of postgraduate training in a U.S. or Canadian program accredited by an organization that is acceptable to the Board

pain_management_education_required.quote: The Board shall require evidence of current professional competence in recognizing the need for timely appropriate consultations and referrals to assure fully informed patient choice of treatment options, including treatments such as those offered by hospice, palliative care, and pain management services.
pain_management_education_required.citation: § 1400. Renewal of license; continuing medical education

telehealth_prescribing_rules.value: Prescribing via electronic means requires: (1) reasonable effort to verify patient identity; (2) documented diagnosis through accepted medical practices; (3) maintenance of a current medical record. An electronic, online, or telephonic evaluation by questionnaire is inadequate for initial evaluation except for medication abortion. Exceptions include initial admission orders for newly hospitalized patients, prescribing for another physician's patient when taking call, prescribing for a patient examined by a licensed advanced practice registered nurse or physician assistant, continuing medication short-term for a new patient prior to first appointment, and emergency situations.
telehealth_prescribing_rules.quote: providing, prescribing, dispensing, or furnishing medical services or prescription medication or prescription-only devices to a person in response to any communication transmitted or received by computer or other electronic means, when the licensee fails to take the following actions to establish and maintain a proper physician-patient relationship

interstate_medical_licensure_compact_mem.quote: The member states hereby create the "Interstate Medical Licensure Compact Commission."

physician_assistant_supervision_model.quote: The Board or the Executive Director of the Board may waive supervision and scope of practice requirements for physician assistants, including the requirement for documentation of the relationship between a physician assistant and a physician pursuant to section 1735a of this title.
physician_assistant_supervision_model.citation: § 1353. Powers and duties of the Board

malpractice_reporting_required.quote: All medical malpractice court judgments and all medical malpractice arbitration awards in which a payment is awarded to a complaining party during the last 10 years, and all settlements of medical malpractice claims in which a payment is made to a complaining party within the last 10 years.

hospital_privilege_action_reporting_requ.quote: A description of revocation or involuntary restriction of hospital privileges for reasons related to competence or character that has been issued by the hospital's governing body or any other official of the hospital after procedural due process has been afforded, or the resignation from, or nonrenewal of, medical staff membership or the restriction of privileges at a hospital taken in lieu of, or in settlement of, a pending disciplinary case related to competence or character in that hospital.

impaired_physician_program_authorized.quote: recommendation or referral for services from the Vermont Practitioner Recovery Network established pursuant to section 1401a of this chapter, or from an employer wellness program or similar program, as a result of a completed, contested disciplinary process
impaired_physician_program_authorized.citation: § 1317. Unprofessional conduct to be reported to Board

compelled_mental_physical_exam_authority.quote: Require a licensee or applicant to submit to a mental or physical examination, and an evaluation of medical knowledge and skill by individuals or entities designated by the Board if the Board has a reasonable basis to believe a licensee or applicant may be incompetent or unable to practice medicine with reasonable skill and safety.
compelled_mental_physical_exam_authority.citation: § 1353. Powers and duties of the Board

scope__license_status_types.quote: Any person who allows a license to lapse by failing to renew the same in accordance with the provisions of this section may be reinstated by the Board by payment of the renewal fee, the late renewal penalty, and if applicable, by completion of the required continuing medical education requirement
scope__license_status_types.citation: § 1400. Renewal of license; continuing medical education

scope__license_status_types.quote: The Board or the Executive Director of the Board may issue a temporary license to an individual who is currently licensed to practice as a physician, physician assistant, or podiatrist in another jurisdiction, whose license is in good standing, and who is not subject to disciplinary proceedings in any other jurisdiction.

In the event of a revocation, the holder of any license or certificate so revoked shall promptly relinquish the license or certificate to the Secretary of the Board.
